Atome Financial is a leading fintech company in south-east Asia that offers buy now pay later services, consumer loans and digital lending services, so this will really boost Grab's financial services division.

thesis: Author is bullish on TransMedics (TMDX) based on Morgan Stanley conference takeaways, citing expected revenue acceleration in 2027-2029 driven by OCS 2.0 approvals for lungs, CHOPS approval, and the massive kidney transplant opportunity. Au
originalText:
Listened to Waleed present at the Morgan Stanley healthcare conference, here are 10 takeaways (some of this we already knew)....
1) 2026 is the big investment year
2) 2027 and 2028 are the big catalyst years which will lead to revenue growth acceleration in 2027, 2028 and 2029
3) They paid mid-single digits (millions) for PAD Aviation, needed to build NOP across Europe in the coming years 
4)  Enhance trials (OCS 2.0 for lungs, approval could come in Q3 or Q4)... will provide access to 600-650 hearts that they don't currently serve with OCS 1.0 which is DBD hearts at 4 hours or less preservation time.
5) DeNovo trial (OCS 2.0 for lungs, approval could come in Q3 or Q4)... will provide access to 450 lungs they don't currently serve with OCS 1.0
6) Will get 510(k) approval for CHOPS which could open up 50% of the transplant market they don't current serve with OCS 1.0 or OCS 2.0
7) Kidney is a massive opportunity for $TMDX -- last year 10,000 kidneys were discarded because of prolonged ischemia / prolonged time on ice, which will get an organ rejected before the surgery or even worse the body rejects it after transplant. Every year CMS spends over $10+ billion on donor list patients, many of these people are waiting for kidneys so throwing away 10,000 of them because we're not preserving / transporting them correctly is inexcusable and expensive. Keep in mind that 50% of organ transplants per year are kidneys and 85% of the people on the transplant list are waiting for kidneys. $TMDX OCS is going to help alot of these people in the coming years and it's very likely they'll save CMS  billions of dollars in the process.
8) Becoming an OPO should drive more growth and efficiency but they won't know until late 2026 or early 2027
9) Europe should start to contribute revenues in 2027, more significant in 2027 2H 
10) Kidney OCS will begin to make meaningful contributions in 2027 2H 

It's possible I've underestimated Kidney because I was thinking that a decent number of transplants came from family members and/or living donors in which case it would be possible to put donor and recipient in the same hospital in which case OCS might not be necessary but that's not what the data suggests. Here are the facts... only 10% of kidney donors are family members and 80% of kidneys are coming from deceased donors in which case they are probably not in the same area as the recipient so these are the kidneys that end up in ice coolers which leads to ischemia and damaged organs thus the 10,000+ discarded kidneys in 2025. 

NFA.
DYOR.

*We are long $TMDX
evidenceSpan: *We are long $TMDX

thesis: Author argues Physical AI will massively expand cloud compute demand, recommending long positions in major AI infrastructure stocks including Microsoft.
originalText:
How to get filthy rich from investing in Physical AI:

Almost everyone, even in AI, is underestimating how big Physical AI will be.

I think AI with a physical embodiment will eventually do the majority of tasks humans currently do in the physical world AND multiply how much physical work we can produce.

It might sound crazy today, but I very clearly see a $100T+ economy here.

Contrary to what many people in the field believe, I think a majority of the compute will very clearly live in the cloud, NOT be on-device.

Some compute might stay on-device: safety, control, privacy, instant reactions.

But the majority of advanced intelligence will live in datacenters.

Compute benefits massively from scale.

Datacenters are gigantic physical systems specifically optimized around power, cooling, networking and utilization. One pool of compute can serve thousands or millions of devices.

On-device compute is the exact opposite: expensive compute dedicated to a single machine, constrained by size, power and cooling.

It will never compete with dedicated datacenters on raw compute or cost efficiency.

Physical AI therefore doesn't reduce the cloud inference opportunity.

It makes it much, much bigger.

$NVDA $NBIS $CRWV $MSFT $AMZN $META $GOOGL $ORCL $TSM $DRAM $SKHY $MU $SNDK will all LOVE Physical AI scaling.

The way to play Physical AI is simple: you stay long almost exactly the same AI infra names, because it's the same companies powering it.

I do believe there will be a few direct physical infra providers like $OUST that will win certain parts of the BOM and have explosive upside potential through technical moats, IP and the purely explosive growth they can face.

But other than that, I think many of the providers will be in a very competitive, low-margin, low-moat battle to be built into these manufacturing processes.

I think many will be bad investments.

Staying long the compute behind it is simple, sexy and will simply work.
evidenceSpan: $NVDA $NBIS $CRWV $MSFT $AMZN $META $GOOGL $ORCL $TSM $DRAM $SKHY $MU $SNDK will all LOVE Physical AI scaling.

Almost everyone, even in AI, is underestimating how big Physical AI will be.

I think AI with a physical embodiment will eventually do the majority of tasks humans currently do in the physical world AND multiply how much physical work we can produce.

It might sound crazy today, but I very clearly see a $100T+ economy here.

Contrary to what many people in the field believe, I think a majority of the compute will very clearly live in the cloud, NOT be on-device.

Some compute might stay on-device: safety, control, privacy, instant reactions.

But the majority of advanced intelligence will live in datacenters.

Compute benefits massively from scale.

Datacenters are gigantic physical systems specifically optimized around power, cooling, networking and utilization. One pool of compute can serve thousands or millions of devices.

On-device compute is the exact opposite: expensive compute dedicated to a single machine, constrained by size, power and cooling.

It will never compete with dedicated datacenters on raw compute or cost efficiency.

Physical AI therefore doesn't reduce the cloud inference opportunity.

It makes it much, much bigger.

$NVDA $NBIS $CRWV $MSFT $AMZN $META $GOOGL $ORCL $TSM $DRAM $SKHY $MU $SNDK will all LOVE Physical AI scaling.

The way to play Physical AI is simple: you stay long almost exactly the same AI infra names, because it's the same companies powering it.

I do believe there will be a few direct physical infra providers like $OUST that will win certain parts of the BOM and have explosive upside potential through technical moats, IP and the purely explosive growth they can face.

But other than that, I think many of the providers will be in a very competitive, low-margin, low-moat battle to be built into these manufacturing processes.

I think many will be bad investments.

Staying long the compute behind it is simple, sexy and will simply work.
evidenceSpan: $NVDA $NBIS $CRWV $MSFT $AMZN $META $GOOGL $ORCL $TSM $DRAM $SKHY $MU $SNDK will all LOVE Physical AI scaling.

thesis: Author shares home workout experience and explicitly discloses buying STRL stock (this week and adding today), constituting a clear position action.
originalText:
Now I know what you all have been raving about. Air conditioning is amazing!!

Have probably done ~800 sessions on this Stairmaster in my home (before gym banned me for using too much, did there). As mentioned yesterday, triple-digit temps in OC forced me to turn on AC and WOW, what a delight now it is to do cardio!

Took this pic 1 hour into it, 430 floors, and I felt like I could go to 1,000 with that ice cool 77 degree air blowing on my back! So luxurious!!

Even though 77 is normally hot at the coast for outside, inside my home is warm due to so much glass and design. If outside is 76, it's 82 or 83 inside and that's with doors and windows open. So 77 was a COLD workout, especially with vent right behind me.

I hope to be rich enough someday to afford AC regularly, but not until $AMZN is $360 and $RKLB is $245 will I even contemplate that.

What you see on TV above was Cramer. Yeah, that's right. I wanted to see $STRL CEO interview on there. As mentioned, I bought this week and another 25 shares today at $476.76.

I've been asked a lot about ideal Stairmaster routine and this is it:

200 floors without touching handles at speed 10 and then 200+ floors with handles at speed 20. Don't ask calorie count, it only counts to 999 then resets.

Oh and make sure you put an $AMZN brown paper envelope over screen, otherwise too depressing to watch. Just pull it back once in a while to peek.

Out of every brand and model, only the 10G from Stairmaster, as it has the widest treads on market at 12". If you are shorter and/or have smaller feet, a lot of other models will work just fine.

Without handles is exponentially harder. If you touch the handles on Stairmaster, you're basically cheating because you're not lifting 100% of your body with just your legs.

I do cheat but only after the non-cheating 200. Always do the hard stuff first.
evidenceSpan: I bought this week and another 25 shares today at $476.76.
activityTitleZH: 分享居家锻炼经历，并明确披露已买入STRL股票（本周及今日加仓），属于明确的持仓行动。
activityTitleEN: Shares home workout experience and explicitly discloses buying STRL stock (this week and adding today), constituting a clear position action.

These 25 new shares of Costco $COST I just bought will almost certainly be CBO'd but nonetheless, bought.

Tax rate in CA is actually above 54.1% when you factor in deductions not allowed at state level, plus the fact I'm due for a penalty, for not being psychic and prepaying 70% of my 2026 income tax by June 15th of this year as required. 

There is no safe harbor in California and the accounting to prove day by day income costs a few thou from CPA. So as it stands now, probably cheaper to pay penalty than prove that I really did pay 70% of my income tax by June 15th.

Stop asking why I live here. Rather, I'll ask you why you live in Florida with a rubbish waveless Atlantic, or muggy, hot, and miserable Texas. Also, weather in Florida sucks and you're on edge for hurricanes yearly vs. rarely like here in CA.

Only places that work for me to live in US are SoCal or Hawaii. That's it, if excluding US island territories. Those I would get island fever and in Hawaii probably too, even Oʻahu.

Though Hawaii does have lower tax burden and it is something loosely being considered on longer term.

Speaking of that state and $COST did you know that Honolulu location is the most profitable Costco store in the world?

$GRAB has seen a dramatic fall in its share price in recent days, but it's getting down to the kind of valuation where I am going to have to consider picking up some more shares.

The forward P/E ratio is now 19.4 and 15.8 for the next two years, with EPS growth expected to be in excess of 13% and 23% in this time.

Furthermore, their free cashflow yield is expected to be 7.92% this year, rising to 12.9% in 2027 and 17.3% in 2028, according to Marketscreener (see below).

thesis: Author believes SNAP is undervalued and predicts a price above $30 in the coming years if the company implements specific structural and operational reforms.

originalText:
I'm not a shareholder but $SNAP does have potential however there are changes that need to happen before any serious investor(s) will buy your stock...

1) get rid of the super voting shares, all shareholders deserve a vote, institutional investors will not touch your stock until this changes 

2) buy some stock in the open market, same with your co-founder, you guys have been nonstop sellers since the IPO, put your money where your mouth is 

3) spinoff SPECS into a new entity with $SNAP shareholders still owning 50-60% considering they've funded this nonsense which has been nothing more than a cash furnace, you can put some cash in and then you can raise cash from VCs - let's see if anyone else is willing to bankroll your hardware vision

4) another 25% headcount reduction, company is still too bloated 

5) reduce SBC which has been out of control since the IPO, you're diluting shareholders more than 10% per year 

6) build a better Board of Directors, you've surrounded yourself with too many spineless people who won't push back 

7) bring in a real CTO because your co-founder is not pulling his weight, I've also heard he's almost never around, your core product has not evolved enough over the past 5 years which is why your monetization is crap for 500M+ daily active users 

8) double down on subscription services because that's one of the best things you guys have done in the past couple years 

9) you need to prioritize ecommerce and live shopping, this could have massive ROI for $SNAP and their biggest influencers 

10) INCREASE GROSS, OPERATING, NET INCOME and FREE CASH MARGINS -- $SNAP was founded 15+ years ago... the company should have at least 30% non-GAAP net income margins by now... if the company wasn't so mismanaged you'd be a FCF machine and buying back your stock right now 

I could keep going but I'll stop there. 

I'm only taking the time to be critical because I believe $SNAP is an undervalued company and could be $30+ in the next few years if you implemented some of these ideas. 

Best of luck. Always happy to chat.
evidenceSpan: I believe $SNAP is an undervalued company and could be $30+ in the next few years if you implemented some of these ideas.

thesis: Author is bullish on NKTR, expecting no deal before trial resolution. Sees a settlement/favorable verdict driving stock to ~$90, followed by a partnership supporting $130-150.
originalText:
To build on this $nktr recent filings (Dkt. 432) confirm the company is actively negotiating the funding and development of rezpeg with multiple parties/ Big Pharma.  This is a live, competitive process. 

I don’t expect a transaction to be announced before the trial resolves, for two reasons.
1, optics before the jury. Any partnership, royalty monetization, or M&A announced mid trial would hand $lly a narrative that $nktt has already been made whole by the return of rezpeg, whatever the legal irrelevance of post breach gains under NY law ($nktr own MIL, Dkt. 430, makes exactly that point). Mgmt has every incentive to keep the deal room closed until a verdict or settlement is in hand.
2, leverage. A settlement adds non dilutive capital and removes the litigation overhang that a partner would otherwise price into terms. $nktr negotiates from a materially stronger position afterward.
So what you’ll see a settlement or favorable verdict first, which I see re rating the stock toward ~$90… then a partnership or strategic transaction, which I see supporting $130-150. Given the competitive process I expect the terms of any deal to be favorable to $nktr
evidenceSpan: I see re rating the stock toward ~$90… then a partnership or strategic transaction, which I see supporting $130-150.
activityTitleZH: 看涨NKTR，认为在诉讼解决前不会达成交易。预计先有和解或有利判决将股价推高至约90美元，随后达成合作支持130-150美元。
activityTitleEN: Is bullish on NKTR, expecting no deal before trial resolution. Sees a settlement/favorable verdict driving stock to ~$90, followed by a partnership supporting $130-150.

thesis: Author reports portfolio update, adding $MU among other stocks to reach 100% allocation, viewing it as an obvious long-term winner.
originalText:
Yes, I still run the @joinautopilot Portfolio!

Should now be at +150% since launch in late March.

Today was the first day in quite a while where I made a bunch of changes.

Cut $BE after it grew to 30% of the Portfolio after quite a crazy rally.

Added some $CRDO and $AVGO since both pulled back quite a bit, clearly are long-term winners and are now chilling at good levels imho. Look technically strong and I can justify the valuations here much better than at their highs.

Then added a lil to obvious winners like $SNDK and $MU to fill up to 100%.

I never tell people to invest in my Autopilot, but today I took a quick look into the investors and WHEN they invested. It's quite comical to be honest to see exactly what you expect to see: people always love to invest AFTER it goes up and hate to deploy funds when it goes down (we rarely do that, but it happens ;D).

Isn't it quite crazy that people just hate the idea of buying things cheap and love buying when everyone buys higher?

This will never change, but it will also always be funny to me.

Pretty sure the average 80IQ "buy the dip" enjoyer outperforms most professional investors by a wide margin.
evidenceSpan: added a lil to obvious winners like $SNDK and $MU to fill up to 100%.

thesis: The author refutes the narrative that AI will replace EDA software, arguing that AI relies on existing proprietary tools and data. They explicitly state they bought 25 shares of CDNS and may add more, indicating a bullish conviction call.
invalidation: AI successfully replicates EDA software or proprietary datasets become accessible to AI models
originalText:
This year, the EDA software duopoly $SNPS and $CDNS keep getting caught in crosshairs of buyable selloffs.

First the SaaSpocalypse.

Second the semis selloff this summer. Since neither Synopsys or Cadence had significantly recovered yet, they were knocked down while still on their knees.

Friday, we got another dump on GPT-6 Astra doing PCB layout in KiCad.

This is a re-hash of the SaaSpocalypse narrative, in that AI will do EDA, so no EDA software is needed!

Sounds logical until you think it through. 

Wouldn't it make more sense for AI to work through existing $SNPS $CDNS software, which is already being done.

Similar to what we're seeing with $NOW, $MSFT, and other platforms declared dead a few months ago?

Better AI does not negate the need for the software, especially when you consider cross-generation designs interoperability, and the patent infringement required for AI to replicate such software.

Though let's say the AI eats software is true and a frontier LLM wants to build their own EDA software. Without the proprietary datasets (PDK in this case) what can the LLM do?

It's not like we're talking generic CRM or HR software, which is not built upon highly secretive proprietary data which $NVDA etc. are not going to be sharing with Anthropic or OpenAI.

https://t.co/nM3vtE6wjS

KiCad PCB layout is not even Synopsys/Cadence business. They make most of their money on IC design.

On Friday I added back 100 shares of $SNPS which I had CBO'd last month. I also added 25 more $CDNS and may add more. Both aren't much higher right now than Friday.
evidenceSpan: I also added 25 more $CDNS and may add more.
activityTitleZH: 反驳AI取代EDA软件的论点，认为AI需要现有软件和数据集，并明确表示已买入25股CDNS且可能继续加仓。
activityTitleEN: Refutes the narrative that AI will replace EDA software, arguing that AI relies on existing proprietary tools and data. They explicitly state they bought 25 shares of CDNS and may add more, indicating a bullish conviction call.

thesis: Author updates portfolio, stating they added to ABVX again this morning, seeing upside potential but not yet at full position size.
originalText:
The Weekly 🌱 
New:
Increased: $cogt, $bhvn , $mrna (s) , $abvx , 
$bcrx 
Unchanged: $cccc, $vera , $kod , $nktr 
Decreased: $abcl (s)
Closed: 

Wild few days in bioland, series of failures for Big Pharma + still very quiet on the deal front. 
I’ve been on vacation the past week , so haven’t done any work on other names but back in east cost and have meetings scheduled + a couple sell side conferences so will be on the lookout for more ideas and commentary. 
$mrna short so far playing out. I think it should settle around $120 in the coming weeks before slowly bleeding once the momentum reverses. Although it has been down 4 out of the last 5 days despite some weird squeezes in the middle. 
I like $cogt , there’s a deficit of good names out there and $Bpmc has been one of the rare acquisitions that’s worked for BP in recent years. So I think it’s a really good deal for whoever acquires them pre or post approval. 
I added $abvx this morning again, let’s see id the recent $lly trip has any real readthrough , still not back to full size obviously because the portfolio composition changed and short selling names takes up  margin which is why I decreased $abcl , I still think it’s overvalued but need to shore up more capital on the long side where most of my names have substantial upside. 
$kod , not happy with how it’s traded but even if daybreak doesn’t impress, you can hold into mesi and they have multiple shots at goal to warrant a higher value. 
$bhvn is interesting I accidentally missed it last time around , but they have a number of updates coming up this month where I think ceo is speaking to sellside and would be looking at any mention of SCA revival. 
$nktr I mean the clearest indication in court documents , this isn’t a small time rumour, literal court filing saying MULTIPLE Big pharma conversations going on.. that’s even more impactful than an FT piece citing multiple sources because it’s not refutable. And it’s active as the documents are as recent as August. 
$vera data and hopefully script data in the coming days, not worried about that position at all. 
$phvs data is solid, and $bcrx obviously trading down on it, but I think it’s oversold here and I added. I was listening to a recent interview of the ceo, I think they’ve been executing really well and have the balance sheet to be aggressive and grow further. This was the last of the overhangs and thus I think upside will return after market moves on from this little hiccup. 
Anyways, $nktr could be a huge winner this month and excited for $mrna short to continue to play out and $kod / $vera data to impress. 
Happy to answer any questions.

activityTitleZH: 加强 ABVX 判断：更新投资组合，表示今早再次加仓ABVX（Abivax），认为其有上行潜力，但仓位未恢复至满仓。

thesis: The author explicitly states a bearish stance on ABNB based on poor personal experiences with independent hotels, advocating for switching to competitors like Marriott and Hilton due to reliability concerns.
originalText:
Pre-covid, $500/night hotel room was nice! Now...

1. TV smaller than your computer monitor.
2. Ants almost anywhere you look.
3. Sewage dripping on your car.
4. Flying cockroaches.
5. Minimal sleep.

Don't I look happy?

The investment takeaways...

This is why I am anti $ABNB and most US independent hotels for stays, preferring to use $MAR, $HLT and own their stocks. I value standards and consistency via franchising enforcement, while being asset-light like Airbnb.

They are too wild west. Questionable cleaning. No gyms and amenities. Shady fees and guest requests, like self-cleaning (which goes back to questionable reliability).

Still hate Rollins $ROL stock but pesticides aren't going away. However just because an industry is safe, doesn't mean it might not carry significant future legal liabilities, which indemnification clauses may not shield.

Oh and as far as that cockroach? Caught it in a clear deli clamshell and gave it to the hotel clerk as a gift last night. She shrieked, in joy I assume.
evidenceSpan: This is why I am anti $ABNB and most US independent hotels for stays, preferring to use $MAR, $HLT and own their stocks.
activityTitleZH: 基于对独立酒店糟糕体验的个人经历，明确看空ABNB，并建议转向拥有标准化服务的竞争对手如万豪和希尔顿。

originalText:
Now that $MU to $SNDK have pulled a major recovery. 

Good to have a reminder that the memory bottleneck hasn’t changed!

Same with CW lasers… substrates… or others.

But short term sentiment (depending on prices/macro) often does.

I think a lot of demand imbalances get worse than people expect:

- There’s some Japanese distributors in Nikkei today saying memory demand deficit has reached 40-60% (67-150% higher than supply). With general prices going up 50% by years end.

- $SPCX isn’t included in the $1.3T hyperscaler capex figures (I think Wells Fargo ets. ~$263b AI capex), so total capex figures might be surprising.

- $SNDK expects 80% gross margins to continue into 2030… (welcome to S&P 100)

- and once again you have long term visibility into 2031 now with companies like Samsung

Memory is very really volatile… some of my positions are up 270%+, so I find it a bit easier to hold through volatile periods.

But regardless, operating fundamentals doesn’t always align with short term price movements.

Same concept can be applied to other sectors.

thesis: Author is bullish on BTDR, believing its Bitcoin mining business is undervalued and will be rerated as BTC prices hold or rise.
originalText:
$BTDR 𝗦𝗼𝗺𝗲𝘁𝗶𝗺𝗲𝘀 𝗜𝘁’𝘀 𝗕𝗲𝘁𝘁𝗲𝗿 𝘁𝗼 𝗠𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗪𝗶𝘁𝗵 𝗖𝗮𝘂𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗧𝗵𝗮𝗻 𝘁𝗼 𝗠𝗼𝘃𝗲 𝗙𝗶𝗿𝘀𝘁

$BTDR is now the world’s largest publicly listed $BTC miner by self-mining hash rate, yet the market is giving it almost no credit for that business because investors believe $BTC recent rally may not be sustainable.

I don’t believe $BTC is going to crash. I believe it will remain around these levels or move higher. Once the market realizes that, $BTDR’s mining operation should be rerated.

Jihan Wu is the smartest CEO in this group in my view. What I like most about him is that he is not in a rush. While everyone else raced to convert electricity into AI data centers and announce enormous contracts, he remained patient.

$CRWV rushed into a low-priced deal with $MSFT that looked impressive in the headlines but required enormous debt and financial commitments. $CIFR also committed its electricity at substantially worse headline economics than the contract $BTDR eventually secured.

In this race, whoever moves first risks locking themselves into the worst economics.

$BTDR currently has approximately 1.75 GW of electricity already online and nearly 3 GW including its development pipeline. That is substantially more operational power today than $IREN. $IREN has assembled a larger future pipeline, but much of it still needs to be developed. There is an enormous difference between electricity that may become available in the future and electricity that is already online today.

$BTDR is choosing to use much of that power for $BTC mining instead of rushing to convert everything into AI data centers. That makes perfect sense.

At current $BTC prices and July’s production rate, $BTDR’s mining operation could generate more than $1 billion in annual revenue and approximately $600–700 million in annual cash profit before corporate expenses, interest and capital expenditure. Why rush to give up that business and commit the electricity for the next 10 or 15 years unless the AI contract is exceptionally attractive?

AI data centers are potentially far more profitable, but $BTDR does not need to convert everything immediately. It can continue mining $BTC, producing cash and waiting until someone offers economics attractive enough to justify surrendering that electricity for the next 10 or 15 years.

That patience is already paying off. $BTDR’s 121 MW Tydal agreement is worth approximately $4.7 billion over 16 years. Its annual headline revenue per MW is roughly 36% higher than $CIFR ’s original Barber Lake agreement. Its 9.5 MW Malaysia facility is also fully committed, representing more than $800 million in expected contracted revenue.

$BTDR also designs and manufactures its own SEALMINER machines. It controls almost the entire chain: electricity, data centers, chips, machines and mining. That allows it to deploy newer and more efficient equipment without depending entirely on outside suppliers.

This is why $BTDR is so compelling. You get the world’s largest publicly listed $BTC mining operation, nearly 3 GW of power, proprietary mining technology and an enormous option on AI data centers.

If $BTC remains around current levels, the mining business deserves a rerating. If $BTC rises, the upside becomes much larger. Meanwhile, Jihan can gradually convert selected sites into AI infrastructure, but only when the economics are clearly superior to mining.

There is no reason to rush. The electricity is not going anywhere.

$BTDR is currently my largest investment in the space at approximately 13% of my portfolio.
evidenceSpan: I believe it will remain around these levels or move higher. Once the market realizes that, $BTDR’s mining operation should be rerated.

originalText:
Yesterday $FCEL reported their Q3 (fiscal year) earnings and the stock fell ~15%.

Let's objectively review the quarter and see whether our thesis is broken or actually got stronger.

But first I really need to address how X is misrepresenting the thesis that me, @babyfolio and @itsalasdairmann have shared around $FCEL.

Our thesis has NEVER been that $FCEL is better than $BE or that FuelCell Energy is a great operator.

Quite the opposite.

We have repeatedly highlighted that this company has historically been poorly managed, destroyed enormous amounts of shareholder capital through dilution and has a terrible execution history.

That is literally WHY the opportunity is asymmetric.

Simple example:

30% chance of +300%
70% chance of -50%
The most likely outcome is still losing money.

But the expected return is +55%.

THAT is asymmetry. These are not $FCEL specific numbers or my expectations, just want to quickly highlight how X doesn't seem to get that the expected outcome for most asymmetric upside stories is actually the stock going down.

Now back to specifics:

The thesis is that AI data centers suddenly created an enormous need for fast, clean, behind-the-meter power.

Fuel cells are one of the few solutions that fit those requirements, while the clear industry leader $BE appears extremely supply constrained.

$FCEL is therefore entering an unusually favorable demand environment at exactly the moment it is trying to massively expand production.

The market already assumes poor execution.

Our upside case does not require FCEL to suddenly become Bloom.

It requires them to execute DECENTLY.

If they can simultaneously:

1. multiply revenue through higher production
2. improve utilization and margins
3. eventually become profitable

you get the combination of accelerating growth + margin expansion that can drive massive reratings.

Of course execution can fail. We have explicitly called execution the single biggest risk from the beginning.

And importantly: I am genuinely not surprised by this earnings reaction.

Before earnings I literally wrote in my trade alerts:

“I would not be surprised if on earnings we go up or down 20%.”

And when I sold:

“Waiting for a cheap bottom-ish price or confirmation above 50SMA or a fundamental catalyst.”

This is exactly why I sold before the print (and to come off margin in bad macro which I don't feel like is predictable right now).

Now let's look at what the quarter actually told us.

WHAT GOT CONFIRMED:

1) Data center demand is very real for them.

FCEL now has the 30MW firm Fit Energy order, another 350MW of awarded capacity, a NEW 75MW paid capacity reservation with a major data center operator and roughly 10GW of active proposals.

Demand risk for their specific solution clearly went down.

2) Pricing is even better than we modeled.

The Fit agreement implies roughly $3.0M/MW of product value versus the ~$2.75M/MW we previously modeled.

3) Customers are willing to pay upfront to reserve FCEL manufacturing capacity.

This is one of the clearest confirmations of the scarcity thesis.

4) The 500MW expansion remains funded and management continues to target June 2028.

The balance sheet is now extremely strong relative to FCEL's history.

WHAT WAS BAD:

1) Current manufacturing economics are worse than I expected.

At only ~37MW annualized production, FCEL's manufacturing costs are currently ABOVE the contractual pricing of the Fit order.

That is the biggest negative from this quarter.

Our thesis assumes higher utilization will dramatically improve unit economics.

Management believes the same thing.

But they have NOT proven it yet.

-> The main negative to me is not that economics are bad at 37MW utilization. That was expected. It's how slowly they appear to be scaling utilization and moving toward profitable economics. That points back to execution

2) The path to profitability is slower/more uncertain than I previously assumed.

Management now targets positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 FY2027 and said it likely requires at least 100MW of actual volume, potentially more.

So simply reaching 100MW manufacturing capacity does not automatically mean profitability.

-> Again, not surprising from an economics POV. The genuinely disappointing part is the lack of speed here. The re-rating journey should be beat and raise, but we get underdeliver and overpromise and delay. Again, bad execution.

3) Most of the $2.35B “awarded backlog” is not yet firm backlog.

It is encouraging because FCEL has been selected for the capacity, but those phases still need to convert into definitive contracts.

-> I would give 0 value to anything that isn't a signed contract. Because we already know the demand is there and massive. The bottleneck is capacity anyway.

4) Execution risk increased.

FCEL now has customers and demand.

The question is whether they can manufacture enough product, cheaply enough, quickly enough.

That is exactly what investors should focus on now.

So my conclusion after the quarter is simple:

The DEMAND side of our thesis got completely validated and at this point just seems to be the known facts on the ground.

The EXECUTION side became more questionable. This is the correct attack angle against the thesis.

I do currently think I was too confident about how quickly enormous demand would translate into attractive margins and profitability.

But this is also where the trading discussion matters!

Weak macro + weak chart + a company with huge execution risk going into a binary earnings event is precisely the kind of setup where I personally think active trading can add value.

Some people make fun of selling a stock you remain bullish on long term. I strongly disagree with that way of thinking.

To me, this quarter is a perfect example of why I do it.

I don't need to sit through every execution miss while waiting years for the thesis to play out.

If FCEL starts proving the business inflection, we can still buy it into strength.

If they don't execute, I simply don't have to re-enter.

And because this is still a relatively underfollowed company where most attention goes to the headline revenue, EPS and stock move, I don't think you need to perfectly bottom-tick it.

If FCEL actually starts converting demand, scaling production and showing margin improvement, there should still be years of growth ahead.

The next major proof point is the 100MW production ramp.

If FCEL reaches that level and unit economics improve dramatically, the rerating thesis remains very much alive.

If they ramp production and margins remain terrible, then we have a much bigger fundamental problem.

For now, FCEL appears to have finally found the market it spent decades waiting for.

Now it has to prove it can actually serve it profitably.

As of today, execution is disappointing to me, but not yet thesis-breaking.

We gave them a 2/5 score on exeuction risk (1 = worst, 5 = best).

Personally, I’ll keep following the company and re-enter if they start delivering. If they don’t, I simply won’t re-enter. It’s that simple.

thesis: Author calculates $80M incremental EBITDA from 20M gallons of renewable LPG sales, implying CLMT is undervalued, a bullish forecast.
originalText:
$CLMT I spent my night mentally obsessing over the 20 million gallons of Renewable LPG that MRL disclosed to us yesterday that they had been burning as fuel gas which they now say is a saleable product.

For HEFA renewable LPG recovered from process off-gas, the incremental EBITDA per gallon is calculated without allocating feedstock cost. Feedstock is purchased and processed for RD + SAF, but the light ends that become renewable propane/LPG are an off-gas streams generated in hydrotreating. When that stream is recovered and sold rather than burned as fuel gas or sent to a hydrogen reformer, the economics are incremental.

Your margin stack proxy is therefore the following:

Mont Belvieu propane = $0.76/gal 

link: https://t.co/lKEwvC2V01

+ 1.1x D5 RIN which is $2.30 = $2.53/gal

https://t.co/3BnU6W39lr

+ .003x $85/Mt LCFS = $0.25/gal

+ $0.50/gal 45z PTC credits

= $4.04/gal Margin

x 20M gals

= $80M annual EBITDA added on top of the $500M mid-cycle @ $2.00/gal RD index + $1 SAF prem.
evidenceSpan: $80M annual EBITDA added on top of the $500M mid-cycle @ $2.00/gal RD index + $1 SAF prem.

thesis: Author argues CRDO's post-earnings drop is misguided, highlights strong future growth, and sees the stock as undervalued, clearly bullish.
originalText:
Another strong report from $CRDO -- https://t.co/vjJhOjxRNX

Stock is probably down AH because the reported $479M revs vs $473M estimates looks like a small beat (and the market wanted more) but the price action is ignoring the massive ramp that is going to happen in the second half of FY2027.

$CRDO just reported their FY2027 Q1:
Revenues were up +114% YoY
Net income was up 141% YoY

When $CRDO reported FY2026 Q4 revs a few months ago they didn't give official FY2027 guidance however on the earnings call management said revenues would be up at least 80% YoY.

Two weeks ago Goldman Sachs met with management and then increased their FY2027 numbers... their new revenue estimate implies 96% YoY 

If we assume Goldman Sachs is closer to the right number for FY2027 (they're probably still leaving room for upside raises), and gross margins stay around 68% and net income margins stay around 50%, then $CRDO should do around $1.3B of net income in FY2027 which means the stock is trading AH at 28x FY2027 EPS with EPS likely growing in the 90-100% range (maybe higher).

I suspect management will give an update on that unofficial FY2027 guidance, might go from "at least 80%" to "at least 85% or at least 90%"

Coming into this print, this is where consensus was on QoQ revenue growth for the next 4 quarters:
Q1 +7.8%
Q2 +9.6%
Q3 +27.1% 
Q4 +23.8%

So, when I say the big ramp is coming in the second half of FY2027, this is what I mean... alot of this is coming from their optics business.  

3 months ago management said "at least 80% growth in FY2027" but now they have more visibility so a bump up on that number means the ramp in 2H will be even bigger than expected. 

Additionally, the massive ai/dc capex buildout from $SPCX over the next 1-2 years could be the wildcard for $CRDO because that growth is definitely not included in current guidance / estimates. 

Finally, I think $CRDO will grow EPS at a ~60% CAGR for the next 3 years so the stock looks very mispriced to me at 28x FY2027 EPS 

NFA
DYOR.

*We are long $CRDO.  .

thesis: The author proposes an options spread on QQQ (buy 715 put, sell 3x 650 puts, sell 750 call) for a $19 credit, expecting the market to fall 5-11% over the next 45 days, representing a clear bearish directional trade.
invalidation: Market rises above 5% or falls more than 11%
originalText:
𝗛𝗢𝗪 𝗧𝗢 𝗛𝗘𝗗𝗚𝗘 𝗬𝗢𝗨𝗥 𝗣𝗢𝗥𝗧𝗙𝗢𝗟𝗜𝗢 𝗥𝗜𝗚𝗛𝗧 𝗡𝗢𝗪?

Before you read this on how I recommend hedging your portfolio in the current environment, first read my previous tweet below it: “What Are You Hedging Against?”

The idea is simple. If your kid rides his bike only inside the house, you probably don’t need to insure it against a total loss. That would be expensive and unnecessary. You insure against the kind of damage that is actually likely to happen.

Same with hedging. First define what you are protecting against. Then build the hedge around that risk.

If everyone is already afraid of a 10% correction and hedge funds have already deleveraged, I struggle to see where the sellers come from for a full 10% drawdown.

But let’s assume they are partially right and we get a correction.

I see four possible outcomes over the next 45 days, into the October 16 expiration:

5% chance: market goes up 5% in the next 45 days

30% chance: The market goes higher. You deleveraged, so you barely participate.

30% chance: The market stays around current levels. Some stocks do well, but because you deleveraged, you probably don’t.

30% chance: We follow the historical pattern and the market corrects, but because everyone is already positioned for it, the drawdown is more like 1% to 7%, not 10%.

5% chance: The market actually falls 10% or more.

Taking that distribution into account, I like a creative hedge/trade on $QQQ into the October 16 expiration:

Buy the 715 put.
Sell 3 puts around 650, roughly 9% lower.
Sell the 750 call, roughly 5% higher.
It’s opened for a $19 credit.

The trade does especially well if the market falls somewhere between roughly 5% and 11%.

The idea is simple: stay exposed to some upside while protecting yourself against the kind of downside I think is actually more likely over the next 45 days.
evidenceSpan: I like a creative hedge/trade on $QQQ into the October 16 expiration: Buy the 715 put. Sell 3 puts around 650, roughly 9% lower. Sell the 750 call, roughly 5% higher. It’s opened for a $19 credit.

thesis: Author is strongly bullish on NBIS, citing differentiated offerings leading to higher rates and better economics, with potential deployment exceeding 8GW by 2031 and asset-light model adding revenue.
originalText:
Walking to a restaurant right now so I'm typing as fast as possible… $NBIS is best in class for many reasons… if their strategy was just to keep doing hyperscaler deals I’d be less bullish but I believe they’re one of the few neoclouds (or neoscalers) that has a truly specialized and differentiated offering whereby they will command higher mid-term and short-rates (for longer) which really changes the economics and then the asset light model should be icing on the cake depending on the size and scope of those deals… I assume it will be a rev share model but details are very limited… once the big hyperscaler contracts have expired, they either get renewed (hopefully at higher rates) or $NBIS has to backfill that capacity with smaller deals (thankfully we don't have to worry about this for 4-5 years)… those GPUs will have been depreciated to zero (or close to it) yet they'll still have residual value making those nextgen contracts significantly more profitable… based on everything I see, hear and read… we are still compute constrained by a meaningful amount… I don’t think that ends anytime soon… not if we’re still in the early innings of ai adoption with token consumption likely growing 100-500x over the next ~5 years… I’m curious how much more upside there might be on MW rates especially on short term deals via spot/auctions… certainly possible we see spot prices hit $60M+ per MW for Vera Rubin but I’d never model those rates into my long term models… I have 9 different models for $NBIS with different inputs for GW deployed by 2031, blended MW rate and share count but generally speaking for my 2031 base case I’m using ~$20M per MW for my blended rate across 5-6GW of deployed compute and that doesn't include anything yet for the asset light business since I have no idea what the economics might look like... $NBIS is guiding to 5GW for 2030... I'm factoring in some small delays along the way but I think there's a good chance that number gets increased by 0.5-1.0GW per year which means by the time we get to 2031 I'm thinking they could be at 8+ GW plus rev share on the asset light strategy (perhaps across 2-6 GW)... will continue to adjust my models as we get more information on capacity, MW rates and the asset light model.

Add it up and my $NBIS base case models for 2031 are in the range of $100-120B revenues with 30-40% ebit margins... of course these numbers will likely be too high or too low... that's why I'll continue to adjust them as we go... my bull case models are using higher numbers for both revenues and ebit margins... in my most bullish model (unicorn) for 2031... I'm at 9GW deployed at $20M per MW with 45% ebit margins and then 3GW on the asset light model (with rev share) at 85% ebit margins... throw a reasonable multiple on that combined ebit number and the $NBIS valuation gets pretty wild. 

Of course there will be headwinds and hurdles over the next 5 years... possible delays in permits, construction and grid connects... bottlenecks in the supply chains and labor shortages... the bears will continue to spread FUD every chance they get... but I'll say this... if ai is the transformational technology that many of us believe it is... and we're still in the early innings of ai adoption... then we're also in the early innings of the ai infrastructure buildout... in which case I believe $NBIS should be a core holding. 

NFA.
DYOR.

*We are long $NBIS
evidenceSpan: I believe they’re one of the few neoclouds (or neoscalers) that has a truly specialized and differentiated offering whereby they will command higher mid-term and short-rates (for longer) which really changes the economics

thesis: Author sees QQQ building a rounding top near 702 with three failed attempts at the same ceiling and deteriorating breadth (negative McClellan Oscillator, shrinking new highs), so leans bearish until breadth confirms price.
invalidation: breadth confirms price (McClellan Oscillator turns positive or participation improves)
originalText:
$QQQ Nasdaq 💻

I am NOT calling for a crash
- but we need to be aware of this distribution

📰 Last two months:
• Nvidia's guidance sparked a tech-only rally 
- $CRM+20% $CRWD $OKTA +9% earnings helped too
— but the Dow only had 6 of 30 stocks green.

• Fed's Warsh flagged sticky inflation heading into Jackson Hole, cooling rate-cut odds.

ROUNDING TOP building since April. 
QQQ has now stalled right under that same rolling dome three separate times since May.

🛎️ 702  is the support  I'm watching 

Now the breadth story, because that's what this chart is really about. 

Breadth measures how many stocks are actually participating in a move, not just what a cap-weighted index dominated by a handful of mega caps is doing. 

The McClellan Oscillator (bottom panel) is a breadth-momentum tool built off the 19-day and 39-day EMAs of NYSE advancers minus decliners. Above zero = broad participation. Below zero = fewer and fewer names carrying the tape, even while price looks fine.

⭐️ Correlation isn't causation 
(but worth watching)

Back in May, the oscillator rolled over into that "no correlation" stretch and QQQ shrugged it off, grinding higher for another month. But in mid-to-late July, that same kind of rollover came right before QQQ's sharpest drop of the summer, straight down into the high-$660s. 

Now it's rolling over a third time, right back at the top of the range — and it's not just this chart. 

The McClellan OSC has stayed negative since mid-August, new 52-week highs across the S&P have shrunk to just 1-4% of members (a healthy market runs 10-12%), and only 54% of stocks are above their 50-day moving average, down from 70% a couple weeks ago.

A third rollover at the same ceiling, with this little participation underneath a near-record print, is what DISTRIBUTION looks like. 

I'm watching 702 closely and leaning bearish here until breadth actually confirms the price.
evidenceSpan: I'm watching 702 closely and leaning bearish here until breadth actually confirms the price.
activityTitleZH: 认为QQQ在702美元附近形成圆顶分布，三次未能突破同一阻力位，且市场广度恶化（麦克莱伦振荡器转负、新高股占比下降），因此看跌QQQ，直到广度确认价格走势。
activityTitleEN: Sees QQQ building a rounding top near 702 with three failed attempts at the same ceiling and deteriorating breadth (negative McClellan Oscillator, shrinking new highs), so leans bearish until breadth confirms price.

thesis: Author sold 80 FN shares on the afterhours earnings jump, expressing bearish view on FN as NVDA proxy due to fragile assumptions and systemic risks.
originalText:
Started writing this day after $NVDA earnings and didn't have time to finish until now:

Interesting though, not the least bit surprising, that a lot of chips and networking names are flattish today while $NVDA rallies. They have very much been inversely correlated lately.

This is why I sold 80 $FN yesterday on the afterhours earnings jump, at $438 to $454. The latter was exact top yesterday afterhours. $ANET, $COHR, $LITE, $CIEN, and so on followed similar pattern.

These are not that +50 I kept from July 29th at $404-409 but rather, the 80 I re-added back last week at $418-419.

Given the CBO on Fabrinet the last month, my net cost after factoring realized gains on the new shares is definitely close to $200, perhaps lower. Not going to bother to calculate exactly.

Given that Fabrinet is direct proxy for NVIDIA, in theory  if you believe $NVDA will do what it hopes, you would actually be buying $FN here as an overlooked and perhaps undervalued way to play it.

I on the other hand, do not question NVIDIA's guidance.

I only question the assumptions it relies on, which requires no shocks to system.

As I had to remind someone this morning, yesterday before their earnings I said $NVDA to $10T is very possible, but it assumes status quo can continue.

Every few years when we get major shocks, most people are flabbergasted and say things like it's a once in century event, so how could they prepare for such a scenario?

The problem with such simple thinking is you are looking at the risks of 1 in a 100 year (or however long) events independently, rather than the cumulative risk of just ONE happening over X period of time.

If any one = same effect on stock or market at whole, why are you only worried about the risk of one, while ignoring others?

Furthermore, many human-induced problems are erratic and first-time in history. Tech of last 100 years wasn't around for 99.999%+ of human history. Only natural events, like earthquakes and geomagnetic storms, are a not if, but when question. Human-induced are more likely ifs.

When you consider all of these together, you realize how much more precarious valuations and longer term financial assumptions are. 

You also realize that, if you want highly lucrative returns, you're not going to get there by just buying great stocks at fair prices or even at their lowest quartile of valuations.

You get there by buying shocks.
evidenceSpan: This is why I sold 80 $FN yesterday on the afterhours earnings jump, at $438 to $454.

activityTitleEN: Sold 80 FN shares on the afterhours earnings jump, expressing bearish view on FN as NVDA proxy due to fragile assumptions and systemic risks.

originalText:
We had a great call with $AAOI management yesterday...  we were very bullish going into the call... we're even more bullish after the call and thus increased our position by approximately ~15%.

Management reiterates that demand is not the problem.. it's all about capacity which is why they're doing the $600M ATM offering... they need to continue increasing capacity for the overwhelming demand they see coming over the next few years. 

It certainly doesn't sound like $AAOI will have any problems hitting their mid-2027 targets (management sounds extremely confident) which implies at least $3.5-4.0B revenues for CY2027. I think there's a decent chance they do $4.5-5.0B revenues next year. 

$AAOI is already sitting on 2 LTAs from hyperscalers and said they could have several more if they had the capacity.  

Reading between lines, seeing another ATM offering and knowing their desire to continue building out capacity in Texas... I'll be surprised if they're not doing at least $550-600M revenues per month by end of 2027 with a decent chance they're doing $650-700M (or more).

Assuming CY2026 revenues come in close to $1.1 billion... I think the odds are increasing that $AAOI does at least 300% revenue growth next year (CY2027) followed by at least 80-120% growth in 2028. 

If $AAOI does $4-5B revenues next year and then on track to double that number in 2028... I fully expect this to be a $500-600 stock in the next 18-24 months.

We own at least 5-6 stocks that I believe can be 5-baggers within the next 2 years... $AAOI is one of them... obviously they need to execute really well and the upside will be significant if they do :)  

NFA.

thesis: Author views Meta's settlement with state AGs as a major clearing event and explicitly states buying 200 shares of META, expressing bullishness.
originalText:
For the first time as long as I've been on X, dare I say I'm now bullish $META stock?

Today’s Meta deal and the 1998 tobacco Master Settlement Agreement (MSA) are the two biggest multi-state AG public health + youth targeting settlements in history. 

They don't match in scale and duration but are quite similar. I generated a side-by-side you can see.

Changes to Instagram and Facebook:

- Default 2-hour daily cap for under-18s (parent can lift it); can drop to 1 hour if rivals sign similar

- Default overnight block (midnight-6 am, expandable to 10 pm-7 am if others join)

- No school-day or late-night notifications for teens

- Hide like/reaction counts for under-18s

- Ban cosmetic/plastic-surgery filters for teens

- Option for a non-personalized feed

- Stronger age assurance, parental tools, faster harmful-content response

-Independent auditor reporting to AGs

Of course the one thing you don't see taken away is infinite scroll. You just know they fought like hell to keep it.

I do think these changes are beneficial for kids, especially the hiding of likes. Though I wish the time restriction was shorter, given infinite scroll remains.

Today serves as a major clearing event for the stock. I added 200 shares of $META however I'm not sure if we hold this bump in the short-term.

Either way, buying today at $570 is small premium vs. a little lower recently with a lot of uncertainty.
evidenceSpan: I added 200 shares of $META
activityTitleZH: 因Meta与州检察长达成和解，认为这是重大利空出清事件，并明确表示已买入200股META，看涨该股。

thesis: Author argues AAOI's drop on ATM offering is overdone as capital will fund capacity expansion to support 2027/2028 growth targets, implying bullish stance.
originalText:
Friday afternoon $AAOI announced a $600M ATM offering... doing this on a Friday at 5pm is definitely frowned upon however if you listened to the $AAOI fireside chat from the Rosenblatt conference last week... this offering should not be a surprise.

Personally I don't think $AAOI should be down ~12% today on ~6% dilution because this cap raise is clearly going to capex which will expand their capacity in Texas to support and possibly surpass their 2027/2028 targets.

Here is some of the Q&A commentary from the fireside chat...

Analyst asks if they're still targeting $471M per month by mid 2027... "Yeah. That's our current expectation. Based on our discussions with customers, the demand is not the limiting factor. We could actually do more revenue than that if we had more capacity at that point or sooner."

This seems pretty clear to me... $AAOI is raising more capital so they can build capacity faster and bigger to capture more of the demand coming in 2027/2028.

With regards to capex, he said... "We are going to continue to make those necessary investments. We said that the back half of the year will be at least as big as the first half of the year. All of that capex is going into production equipment and machinery, a little bit into R&D and some into real estate to support this additional production capacity"

He said the ROI for this capex is 9-10 months.

He said... "as long as we continue to see demand and we have capital available, I'll make those investments all day long."

He said the biggest risk right now is not moving fast enough or being aggressive enough with increasing capacity which means customers might go somewhere else. "If another customer came to us, and some have, and said 'we need x number of units'... We would have to say "sorry, we are sold out through second half of next year and beyond" .

Obviously no shareholder likes dilution and ATM offering announcements on a Friday afternoon is less than ideal but it's pretty clear to me this company is raising capital to continue building capacity so they can ramp revenues to $450-550M per month by mid 2027 and $550-650M per month by end of 2027 which means 2028 could be $7-9B which is 20x growth from just a couple years ago.

If you want to own a company that can grow revenues by 10-20x over 2-3 years... well then you should probably expect some dilution along the way. The best hypergrowth stories can get pretty bumpy and frustrating but these pullbacks create buying opportunities for long-term investors.

I'll gladly take 6% dilution if it means $AAOI has a better chance of hitting the numbers I mentioned above. Someday they'll have enough OCF/FCF to finance additional capex but they're not there yet.

Hopefully this is the last offering for at least 3-6 months.

NFA.
DYOR.
evidenceSpan: Personally I don't think $AAOI should be down ~12% today on ~6% dilution because this cap raise is clearly going to capex which will expand their capacity in Texas to support and possibly surpass their 2027/2028 targets.

activityTitleEN: Argues AAOI's drop on ATM offering is overdone as capital will fund capacity expansion to support 2027/2028 growth targets, implying bullish stance.

thesis: Author reaffirms bullish stance on ABVX, maintains largest position, and considers shifting some equity to options to address trading dynamics.
originalText:
The Weekly 🌱 
New: 
Increased:  
Unchanged: $cccc, $nktr , $tenx , $vera
Decreased: $bcrx , $abvx 
Closed: $iva , $lqda (s) 

Another week, another weekly. For the first time, I was a net seller of $abvx equity. The longer this has dragged on (no M&A), the more abuse has been hurled at me. Which is fine, when you put yourself out there it’s normal, I was a pro athlete before so it’s not my first rodeo in understanding you cannot make everyone happy and being resilient around but not ignorant to criticism . 
Although I don’t need to, it’s very important for me to address that I remain bullish $abvx and it remains my largest position but I did get it wrong in terms of the trading dynamics. Whilst I knew the name would never just go from 130.140.150.160 and so on ( $rvmd style) I also did not expect it to trail the $xbi so heavily. The stock has a divergence of ~25% vs $xbi from the 2nd of July which was when the offering closed following one of the biggest derisking events in the companies history. This sort of irrational behaviour presents an opportunity where the r/r has shifted, and LEAPS / using of derivatives may be the play keeping CD in mind next year as solely leaning on equity which has being faring terribly whilst the in flows into biotech continue to grow. (Note: it’s something I am contemplating and I’ve spent the weekend reviewing the best strategy from both a long and short term perspective) 
If I really was “misguiding” anyone , I had 4 opportunities to sell prior, which included when Marc came on BiotechTV and practically confirmed no near term M&A. When $abvx categorically denied $azn rumours. Pre maintenance derisking when I knew the scrutiny would be high as everyone was looking at it very closely. And post part 2 when basically heavily levering up post crash meant it was justified to reshuffle the risk. I remained bullish and remain bullish. I’m conscious that publicly sharing my views while managing my own book comes with a duty to be straight about both.
 
Also the price action or my decision to shift out of some of the equity to options doesn’t change the probability of M&A which is the bull case short term and or the probability of a Crohn’s hit. 
For $lqda $crvs $sls $capr etc bulls / cultists , I jump in where I see an opportunity, present my case for public scrutiny, I personally don’t have anything against anyone. It’s the stock market.. stocks go up they go down. I didn’t drop $lqda from $90 to $69… but did I profit from it yes! Same with $crvs , although they literally had to jump on a sell side call to address my points in my short thesis stock tanked from $22 to $12 which would mean that my research carried substance. I don’t just say things unless i genuinely believe them, and my belief leads my portfolio decisions not the other way around. 
Two of my names have impending catalysts $vera and $nktr , and my strength upon reflection lies investing around these catalysts. My M&A trades have actually had a negative return. $cdtx was the only exception over many years but you could still justify holding that through the ph3 data. (Ps I’m still holding $abvx for CD).    
$iva I sold because I’m a little hesitant to trade another pure binary after $tenx but I still think it hits. (Again the research and portfolio management don’t always have to swing the same way)  
I’ll continue to share ideas, a few bad eggs will not deter me and I back myself to be right more often than not. And in that process if I can continue to positively impact lives, that is what motivates me everyday. 
Let’s see what next week brings. Remain available to answer questions.

We need much more Fuel Cells and comparable BTM AI power solutions, NOW!

thesis: Author views NBIS's convertible raise terms as favorable, dismisses dilution fears, and is bullish on future ARR growth, advising to hold.
originalText:
$NBIS convert raise terms are out!

Facts:

Nebius upsized the deal from $4.5B to $5.0B, with an option to reach $5.75B. Net proceeds are ~$4.94B, or ~$5.68B with the option exercised.

$3B due 2030: 0.50% coupon, $313.46 conversion price, +40% premium.

$2B due 2034: 4.50% coupon, $324.65 conversion price, +45% premium.

Including principal accretion, effective conversion prices at maturity are ~$345 and ~$406.

The money is explicitly  (and obviously) going toward data centers, GPUs, footprint expansion and the AI cloud.

If the full $5B new convert were eventually settled entirely in shares, it represents ~15.7M shares. Nebius can also settle in cash or a mix, so that dilution is NOT guaranteed.

They are also exchanging $800M of old converts for ~15.8M shares, but those old notes already represented ~15.55M potential shares. 

!! So most of that “dilution” was already embedded !!

tl;dr expected raise, good terms, onwards.

Not sure why people pee their pants because of this 😂

We learned that their economics / MW are amazing. Now let them build the MW! That costs money.
They want to build A LOT.

The shareholders that cry today are the same people that will laugh because of the ARR growth soon.

As long as you don't sell lol
evidenceSpan: The shareholders that cry today are the same people that will laugh because of the ARR growth soon. As long as you don't sell lol

- Hydrogen production
- Water desalination
- Power supply for energy-intensive users such as data centers

Transcript excerpt:
当前市场出现回调，SPY在创下历史新高后形成新的看跌蜡烛线。这一走势是否预示顶部信号？若后续继续回调，又该如何应对？本视频将深入分析实用的交易策略，帮助散户投资者在当前市场中把握机会。目前SPY的1小时图仍保持极度看涨形态，持续创出更高高点与更高低点，并始终位于上升的21小时均线之上。只要这种结构不被破坏，短期内不会出现有意义的反转，因此日线级别的显著回调也难以形成。

关键在于观察SPY是否跌破今日低点及21小时均线。一旦确认失守，将构成明确的顶部信号，可能引发进一步调整，目标位指向760区域的双重支撑区——该位置此前为阻力位，现已转为技术支撑。此外，21日均线也被视为未来潜在支撑位，但当前应优先关注760附近这一关键区域。值得注意的是，单根蜡烛无法构成有效反转信号，必须等待更多确认。

同样地，QQQ在突破昨日高点后回落，1小时图尚未重新测试21小时均线，整体仍处于看涨区间，维持更高高点与更高低点结构。若未来出现跌破今日低点及21小时均线的情况，则可能触发更明显的回调，目标位或下探至701.59（即前期缺口位置）及21日均线附近。该缺口也可能在未来成为支撑水平。

尽管市场出现短期回调，但所有标的如SPY、QQQ、Nvidia等均保持整体看涨趋势。即使出现回撤至支撑区，也可能是暂时性修正，而非趋势终结。任何在支撑位获得确认的看涨反弹，都将提供新的买入机会。尤其对于Nvidia而言，其走势已远超预期，目标价已突破原定的214，正朝着更高目标推进。

Nvidia当前表现极为强劲，已突破关键阻力位214，进入新一轮上涨通道。根据策略建议，当股价触及目标价时，应部分获利了结，例如卖出50%至70%仓位。同时设置214的追踪止盈，一旦跌破此关键点位，即触发止损，锁定利润。此举既能避免错失上涨空间，又能防范潜在回调风险。

从风险收益比来看，此前止损设于189，目标为214，现目标已提升至236，整体回报率极具吸引力。若最终抵达终极高点，可考虑在236完成全部平仓。214是Nvidia最重要的技术转折点，一旦失守，可能意味着假突破或波动性驱动的“牛市陷阱”，随后可能回撤至21日均线甚至200区间。因此，该价位是必须紧盯的核心支撑。

自6月20日首次买入信号以来，我们多次在214附近进行买卖操作，验证了该位置的长期有效性。通过严格执行风险管理与交易策略，可有效消除交易中的四大恐惧：亏损恐惧、错失良机恐惧、落袋为安恐惧、犯错恐惧。当前策略正是通过部分止盈与保留头寸，实现风险控制与机会捕捉的平衡。

特斯拉当前下跌1.77%，但已反弹至297附近支撑位，该位置为此前买入点。目标价仍为342，若1小时图显示回测21小时均线，则为正常回调。若跌破今日低点及21小时均线，可能引发更深调整，目标或下探至297。不过目前仍处于健康运行状态，未见明确反转信号。

AMD今日下跌7%，收复前期缺口，形成顶部信号。若能进一步回落，接近支撑区则更具投资价值。理想情况下，应在支撑位附近出现看涨反应，以获取更优的风险收益比。但当前尚未出现此类信号，且未靠近支撑区，因此暂不构成买入条件。建议观望，等待更清晰的入场机会。

Palantir近期在报告后形成顶部信号，位于关键阻力区下方。该位置为长期形成的双阻力位，此前多次作为交易目标。我们曾多次在此区域买卖，表明其重要性。若未能在支撑区企稳，可能继续回调至136或21日均线，甚至完全回补缺口。因此，当前不宜买入，但若认为过热，可在阻力区选择卖出，合理设置止损与目标，才是专业交易者应有的做法。

Irene（IREN）今日收出看跌蜡烛，收盘低于当日低点，若明日确认跌破21日均线，将强化回调信号，目标位为30至32美元之间的双重支撑区。若能回升并突破21小时均线，创出新高，则可避免熊市情景。当前处于敏感阶段，需密切关注下一波突破方向。若向上突破42美元，则可能开启新一轮上涨，目标或上探60美元。

SanDisk在财报后盘后大跌，再次形成顶部信号，且面临21日均线的强阻力。当前价格已开始回补缺口，1小时图显示接近短期支撑位。若继续下行，跌破支撑，将确认熊市延续，目标位为998（约1000美元整数关口）。目前仍处于低于21日均线、低点不断降低的状态，缺乏反弹迹象，因此不建议介入，待更明确的企稳信号出现后再考虑。
